title: A note on connections between the Föllmer process and the denoising diffusion probabilistic model

paper.title: A note on connections between the Föllmer process and the denoising diffusion probabilistic model
paper.abstract:
Abstract The Föllmer process is a Brownian motion conditioned to have a pre-specified distribution at time 1.
This process can be interpreted as an “augmented” time-compressed version of the reverse stochastic differential equation (SDE) for the denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM).
While this fact has been indirectly used to analyze DDPM sampling errors via discretization of the reverse SDE, connections between direct discretization of the Föllmer process and the DDPM sampler have not yet been fully explored.
This note aims to clarify this point while surveying relevant results from existing work.
We show that discretized Föllmer processes give natural hyper-parameter settings of the DDPM sampler.
Moreover, this allows us to systematically recover state-of-the-art results on DDPM sampling error bounds with slight improvements. Keywords :
diffusion model,
discretization,
low-dimensional adaptation,
sampling error,
score-based generative modeling,
stochastic localization.

Following [ 17 ] , we call a d d -dimensional continuous stochastic process X = ( X t ) t ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] X=(X_{t})_{t\in[0,1]} the Föllmer process associated with μ \mu if X 1 ∼ μ X_{1}\sim\mu and the conditional law of X X given X 1 X_{1} is the d d -dimensional Brownian bridge from 0 to X 1 X_{1} on [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] . This process has recently received renewed attention in various fields of both theory and application such as studies of functional inequalities [ 38 , 18 , 17 , 16 , 46 , 45 , 36 ] as well as high-dimensional central limit theorems [ 19 , 21 , 22 ] , optimization [ 9 , 43 ] , generative modeling [ 5 , 59 ] , sampling from probability distributions [ 55 , 30 , 61 , 20 ] and Bayesian inference [ 57 , 52 ] . Historically, the Föllmer process appeared as the solution to an entropy minimization problem posed by Schrödinger. A modern formulation of Schrödinger’s problem is as follows (see [ 39 , 44 ] for more details). Indeed, we will show that X X always solves ( 1.2 ) without any assumption on μ \mu ; see Theorem 2.1 . ∇ log ⁡ p t \nabla\log p_{t} is known as the score function of (the law of) X t X_{t} , and the form of ( 1.2 ) reminds us of the SDE formulation of score-based generative modeling (SGM) in Song et al. [54] . In fact, it turns out that X X is an “augmented” time-compressed version of the reverse SDE corresponding to the denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) of [ 29 ] ; see Proposition 3.1 . Although this fact is essentially known in the literature (see the discussion preceding Proposition 3.1 ), existing work does not seem to fully explore connections between discretization of the Föllmer process and the DDPM sampler. This note aims to clarify this point while surveying relevant results in the literature. As we will see in Section 3 , discretized Föllmer processes give natural hyper-parameter settings of the DDPM sampler. In addition, we can systematically recover state-of-the-art results on DDPM sampling error bounds in [ 3 , 8 , 31 ] , along with slight improvements. The key to our development is the fact that the Föllmer process is strongly linked to some information-theoretic quantities and Eldan [15] ’s stochastic localization. Indeed, these links were implicitly used in [ 3 , 31 ] to analyze discretization errors of the reverse SDE in SGM. Our development complements these works. While the Föllmer process has been already used for generative modeling as mentioned above, most studies have used it for developing an alternative model to the DDPM rather than analyzing the DDPM itself. In fact, Chen et al. [5] and Wang et al. [59] employ the Föllmer process as a part of more sophisticated generative models proposed therein. We also remark that a solution to the problem ( 1.1 ) in the general case, known as the Schrödinger bridge , is extensively employed for generative modeling. Among others, its connection to SGM is discussed in [ 12 , 4 , 6 , 49 ] . However, the focus of these studies is to develop a more general framework than SGM. 1 1 1 Note that Chen & Vanden-Eijnden [6] use the term “Föllmer process” to indicate the Schrödinger bridge whose initial marginal μ 0 \mu_{0} is the Dirac measure. The remainder of this note is organized as follows. Section 2 reviews basic properties of the Föllmer process. Section 3 discusses its connection to the DDPM, with emphasis on its implication to sampling error evaluation. The appendix presents additional mathematical proofs.

This process can be interpreted as an “augmented” time-compressed version of the reverse stochastic differential equation (SDE) for the denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM). While this fact has been indirectly used to analyze DDPM sampling errors via discretization of the reverse SDE, connections between direct discretization of the Föllmer process and the DDPM sampler have not yet been fully explored. This note aims to clarify this point while surveying relevant results from existing work. We show that discretized Föllmer processes give natural hyper-parameter settings of the DDPM sampler. Moreover, this allows us to systematically recover state-of-the-art results on DDPM sampling error bounds with slight improvements. As we will see in Section 3 , discretized Föllmer processes give natural hyper-parameter settings of the DDPM sampler. The key to our development is the fact that the Föllmer process is strongly linked to some information-theoretic quantities and Eldan [15] ’s stochastic localization. Indeed, these links were implicitly used in [ 3 , 31 ] to analyze discretization errors of the reverse SDE in SGM. Our development complements these works. While the Föllmer process has been already used for generative modeling as mentioned above, most studies have used it for developing an alternative model to the DDPM rather than analyzing the DDPM itself. In fact, Chen et al. [5] and Wang et al. [59] employ the Föllmer process as a part of more sophisticated generative models proposed therein. We also remark that a solution to the problem ( 1.1 ) in the general case, known as the Schrödinger bridge , is extensively employed for generative modeling. Among others, its connection to SGM is discussed in [ 12 , 4 , 6 , 49 ] . However, the focus of these studies is to develop a more general framework than SGM. 1 1 1 Note that Chen & Vanden-Eijnden [6] use the term “Föllmer process” to indicate the Schrödinger bridge whose initial marginal μ 0 \mu_{0} is the Dirac measure.
